messages:
Nina: FYI — I'm putting up a short proposal for trace TTLs: dynamic promotion of spans to a hot tier when they indicate errors/SLO breaches. Want quick reactions before I write an RFC.

Rahul: Clarify: per-service default TTLs and then per-span overrides based on attributes? or fully per-tenant?

Nina: per-service default (env-level overrides) + per-span promotion when attribute `error=true` or `http.status_code>=500` or when sampling_score > 0.8. Goal: keep high-fidelity traces for incidents without keeping everything in hot storage.

Tom: How do we implement promotion with our OTEL pipeline? tail-sampling can help, but routing/exporter decisions are the tricky bit.

Maya: We can do attribute-based routing in the collector. Example prototype config snippet: 
```yaml
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: errors
        decision_wait: 30s
        rules:
          - attribute:
              key: error
              value: "true"
exporters:
  hot_storage:
    endpoint: https://traces-hot.redwood
  cold_storage:
    endpoint: https://traces-cold.redwood
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [tail_sampling]
      exporters: [cold_storage] # default
      # promoted spans forwarded only to hot_storage by the processor
```
This avoids blindly duplicating every span to both stores.

Rahul: Nice. Concern: if promoted spans only go to hot, cold loses the full stream. For compliance/regulatory we might need a cold archive of everything. Do we keep a sampled cold copy or full?

Eli: For Dedicated / Private deployments we must respect customer retention SLAs and data residency (EU customers may require long-term archival). We should separate the "hot" promotion flow from the legal cold archive. Cold archive could be lower-replica / compressed and only used for rehydration.

Nina: Proposal: hot = high-availability, quick-query tier (90d by default for prod errors), cold = compressed archive (30d default, plus separate long-term archival export for regulated customers). Promotion should not cause unbounded duplication — we either move (hot only) and store minimal pointer in cold, or keep cold sampled + hot full.

Tom: UX question: Console settings — how do teams configure this safely? per-environment toggle? per-service policy? I think per-service with environment inheritance + a preview of estimated cost delta.

Maya: Console should present: current ingest rate, projected hot promotion rate (based on last 30 days), and estimated storage/cost change. Also a canary rollout option: enable for 5% of traces or only for traces with severity >= X.

Rahul: Also need to think about dedupe and trace reconstruction if we reingest to hot. Use a deterministic trace_id and add `_storage_tier` attribute so query engine can dedupe.

Eli: Query layer: if a trace isn't found in hot, fall back to cold retrieval path (higher latency). We should add a transparent fallback and show a badge in UI when a trace was reconstructed from cold.

Maya: Ops concern — promoting spans could increase write QPS to hot store during incidents. We need autoscale policies and throttles (circuit breaker) to avoid thundering herd. Also telemetry of promotion rate itself.

Nina: Good point. We'll add a global rate cap and per-service soft limits; Console will surface when a service hits soft limit.

otel-collector-bot: heads-up — collector v0.58.0 adds exporter routing & attribute-based forwarding (use `forward_to` processor).

Tom: That helps. Action items: @Maya prototype collector pipeline + sample config, @Tom mock Console policy UI + cost preview, @Rahul run cost sims for top 10 services (last 90d) with a 5/25/50% promotion rate, @Eli map regulatory retention requirements per-region. I'll schedule a 30m sync Thurs 10am.

Nina: thanks — I'll draft the RFC after the prototypes. :thumbsup:
